correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the published exact local formula for \(\nu_p(\sigma(q^a))\). For \(p=5\), the only multiplicative orders are \(1,2,4\), giving the three stated trigger classes. The level-one statement follows because global valuation is a sum of nonnegative local valuations; the mod-\(25\) exclusions are exactly the cases where the local cyclotomic factor acquires a second factor of \(5\). The density proof bounds the exceptional set by simultaneous even-valuation conditions at primes \(q\equiv4\pmod5\), whose finite-set densities multiply to \(\prod q/(q+1)\), tending to zero by the classical divergence of reciprocal primes in that arithmetic progression. The packaged verifier reproduces the exact valuation for every \(n\le200000\).

value.rationale: The focal paper explicitly singles out the \(p=5\) characterization as an interesting question. The theorem answers that natural question completely by three residue/exponent triggers, sharpens it to an exact first-valuation classification modulo \(25\), and shows that divisibility by \(5\) occurs for a density-one set of integers. This is a complete structurally motivated classification rather than an arbitrary slice or a finite-table recomputation.
